text: I have never seen a worse paper. <break time="0.8s" /> In my life for it is one of those sprawling, flamboyant patterns. <break time="0.8s" /> That commit every artistic sin. <break time="0.8s" /> Its lame, uncertain curves. <break time="0.8s" /> When you follow them. <break time="0.8s" /> For a little distance suddenly plunge off. <break time="0.8s" /> At outrageous angles. <break time="0.8s" /> And destroy themselves. <break time="0.8s" /> In unheard of contradictions. <break time="0.8s" /> The color is repellent. <break time="0.8s" /> Almost revolting. <break time="0.8s" /> A smouldering, unclean yellow. <break time="0.8s" /> Strangely faded by the slow turning sunlight. <break time="0.8s" /> And in some places. <break time="0.8s" /> The paper has been stripped off. <break time="0.8s" /> In great patches. <break time="0.8s" /> John is very careful and loving. <break time="0.8s" /> And he hardly lets me stir. <break time="0.8s" /> Without special direction. <break time="0.8s" /> For he has a schedule prescription. <break time="0.8s" /> For each hour in the day. <break time="0.8s" /> I feel basely ungrateful. <break time="0.8s" /> Not to value his care more. <break time="0.8s" /> Yet John does not know. <break time="0.8s" /> How much I really suffer. <break time="0.8s" /> For he knows. <break time="0.8s" /> There is no reason to suffer. <break time="0.8s" /> It is fortunate. <break time="0.8s" /> That Mary is so good with the baby. <break time="0.8s" /> Such a dear baby. <break time="0.8s" /> And yet I cannot be with him myself. <break time="0.8s" /> For it makes me so nervous. <break time="0.8s" /> When I asked John. <break time="0.8s" /> To repaper the room. <break time="0.8s" /> He said. <break time="0.8s" /> That if he gave in the heavy bed would come next. <break time="0.8s" /> Then the barred windows. <break time="0.8s" /> And then the gate at the stairs. <break time="0.8s" /> His sister Jennie. <break time="0.8s" /> A perfect and enthusiastic housekeeper. <break time="0.8s" /> Who hopes for no better profession. <break time="0.8s" /> Keeps the house for us. <break time="0.8s" /> And thinks it is the writing. <break time="0.8s" /> Which made me sick. <break time="0.8s" /> Meanwhile, the paper stares at me. <break time="0.8s" /> As if it knew. <break time="0.8s" /> What a vicious influence it had with two bulbous eyes. <break time="0.8s" /> That look at me upside down.
